title: Communication in Geriatrics – The importance of Elderspeak for older people
summary:
Effective and respectful communication is essential for the quality of care for older people in the healthcare sector. Especially in communication between medical staff and geriatric patients, the way in which language is used plays a decisive role. In view of the demographic change in our society, the inpatient treatment of older patients will become increasingly important in the future. It is therefore all the more important to constantly review the quality of medical care and strive for improvements. Part of the quality of care is the communication between patients and hospital staff. Age stereotypes can lead to linguistic overadaptation (Ryan et al., 1995). This communication overadaptation has been referred to as elderspeak since 1986 and includes, among other things, simplified language, slow speech and the excessive use of terms of endearment (Cohen & Faulkner, 1986; Caporael, 1983; Sachweh, 1998; Whitbourne et al., 1995). Since then, various studies have dealt with the topic and investigated characteristics of elderspeak and possible causes, but mostly from the perspective of speakers such as nursing staff (Sachweh, 1998; Thimm et al., 1998; Edwards & Noller, 1998; Hehman et al., 2012). The aim of this study is therefore to use video sequences to investigate whether older patients notice the Elderspeak elements in the videos, which language style they prefer (Elderspeak versus neutral language), and how the Elderspeak elements make them feel. Various videos were created to illustrate a typical clinical situation between nursing staff and patients. Video 1 contains a neutral language style without Elderspeak, while video 2 shows various elements of Elderspeak (collective pronouns, diminutives, exaggerated prosody). The visual and auditory presentation of the phenomenon is a novelty in German-language elderspeak research. 
The videos are first played to the study participants. They then receive a questionnaire containing specific questions to assess the perceived differences, preference and possible effects on their well-being. In addition, socio-demographic data and data from the geriatric assessment (functionality, mobility, cognition, depression, social status) are collected. This data will be used to identify patient-related factors that may influence the perception of Elderspeak. These include, in particular, socio-demographic information such as gender and level of education as well as health factors such as mood. With regard to the results, it can be assumed that the test subjects prefer the variant without elderspeak components and that the elderspeak variant is even negatively associated with their well-being. It is also expected that individual factors such as gender and education level could have an influence on the perception of Elderspeak. By understanding how older people perceive Elderspeak, we can improve the quality of their healthcare in the future and minimize the negative effects of Elderspeak.

interventions.name:
Geriatric patients are included in the study during their inpatient stay in two hospitals in Saxony-Anhalt (Germany).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients without cognitive deficits relevant to everyday life (MMSE score 25-30)
- Patients without severe hearing or vision impairment
- Patients with sufficient knowledge of the German language
- Patients who provide written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with cognitive deficits relevant to everyday life (MMSE score < 25)
- Patients with severe hearing and vision impairments that affect the perception of the video sequences
- Patients who do not have sufficient knowledge of the German language to recognize the linguistic differences in the videos
- Patients diagnosed with dementia or a condition that impairs the ability to consent
- Patients who refuse to participate in the study
